punchline: Zamperini survived 47 days on a raft, and the war was still following him home.
thirty_sec: Louis Zamperini, an Olympic runner, survived a Pacific bomber crash and 47 days adrift on a raft before being taken prisoner by Japanese forces. He lived through about two years of camps, where a guard called the Bird targeted him. Back home he was full of anger. In 1950 he went to a prison in Tokyo to meet former guards. Laura Hillenbrand tells this in Unbroken.
